- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 2-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.5) and price is trending up, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–2% and avoid sharp upward revisions.
- Model tends to overpredict in early forecast horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is volatile; use 3-day weighted average for first 3 days.
- If sentiment is flat (0.4–0.6) and price is near mean, model often drifts toward overprediction; apply mean reversion rule: forecast = prior 5-day average ± 1.5% of range.
- For long-term (10+ day) forecasts, model often underestimates if sentiment is weak; add 0.5–1.5% per day to forecast if sentiment <0.4 for 3+ days.
- If sentiment is rising and price is falling, model often misreads momentum; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment reversal within 2–3 days.
